newsitem.title: USA: New allegations on Centennial ex-CEO - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: New allegations on Centennial ex-CEO - WSJ.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission is probing claims that Centennial Technologies' former chief executive was fired once before for allegedly inflating a company's profits, the Wall Street Journal said Friday.

The paper said a former marketing director for Singer Co has told the SEC that Emanuel Pinez was fired from Singer after the company suspected him of booking sales for which he had not received money.

The Singer director, George Chamberlain, told the paper that a raid of Pinez's offices at Singer in 1971 uncovered invoices that had been recorded on the company's financial statements but were never sent to customers.

Pinez was fired from Centennial on February 11 after the company began an investigation into the accuracy of its financial results. He has been in federal custody pending charges of insider trading, manipulating inventory and overstating revenue.
